FR-DUPLICATE.interpretation: September2009 section2: accepted pure ACK, outstanding data, no SYN/FIN/text, ACK=UNA, wire window equals last accepted ACK-bearing wire window. Invalid/future segments ignored; window updates/data/FIN do not increment. Positive window and no persist are explicit scope guards. Counts reset on new UNA, actual congestion RTO, no flight or connection cleanup.

FR-RETRANSMIT.interpretation: Section3.2 steps2/3: third duplicate ACK retransmits oldest prefix without consuming sequence space or waiting for RTO; ssthresh=max(floor(FlightSize/2),2SMSS), cwnd=ssthresh+3SMSS. Extra duplicate ACK inflates by SMSS without retransmitting again.

FR-EXIT.interpretation: Section3.2 step6: first ACK advancing UNA exits Reno, deflates to ssthresh, clears CA credit without extra SS/CA growth. Partial ACK exits too: not NewReno. Actual congestion RTO leaves recovery with parent loss window.

FR-KARN.interpretation: Section3 Karn ambiguity applies also to fast retransmission. Update actual per-byte send times and overlapped sample ambiguity; do not increment RTO retries/backoff or relabel fast recovery as timer retransmission. Keep existing RTO deadline; parent byte-age rule defers an early expiry after the fast send.

FR-SCOPE.interpretation: MSS4/queue16; explicit app.transmit new-data scheduling; no limited transmit, automatic new-data emission on each duplicate, idle restart, ECN/SACK/NewReno, FIN-only fast recovery or complete TCP proof. Legacy FIN lacks wire window and invalidates last-window knowledge.

CC-SCOPE.interpretation: Parent budget, growth, timeout and persist properties retained; this overlay adds explicit finite Reno recovery. Remaining exclusions are preserved in model scope and source documentation.
